title: Authority boundaries from source to publication
summary: Legal Interrogation is an authoring and cross-examination layer upstream of Legal Effect. Its compile handoff is deliberately non-authoritative. Legal Effect verifies source/provision evidence and compiles/certifies the generation. Institutional Policy may then select and publish the exact reviewed artifact.
invariants: Legal Interrogation must not mint compiler authority or fabricate LegalCompileProposal authority.
Only the Legal Effect compiler/certification path may produce an authority-bearing legal generation.
A manually proposed or model-generated proposition remains a proposal until it passes the required challenge, evidence and compiler boundaries.
Institutional Policy may govern publication/effective lifecycle but must not impersonate legal semantics.
Organisational policy may be stricter than law; outputs must preserve the distinction between legal prohibition and institutional-policy prohibition.

provenance.claim: Legal Effect v0.14 owns structured legal-effect evaluation and the compiler/certification authority boundary; public legal API remains legal.effect/0.10.
Institutional Policy owns fixed/versioned publication identity, authority, effective time, lifecycle, topology, rollout and replay rather than domain legal semantics.
Legal Interrogation dev5 implements clause interrogation, proposition challenge, lifecycle invalidation and a real Intention Service dev11 discovery adapter.
